apps.name: Dylan's Baritone Ukulele
apps.subtitle: Chords and notes for baritone uke
description: A baritone ukulele (tuned D G B E, like a guitar's top four strings) that you play with your finger. Tap spots on the neck to press the strings: it plays each note and tells you, in plain English, which chord you've made.
Below the neck are 21 common chords and every note the neck can play. Tap one to hear it, see how to finger it, and put it on the neck.
features: A neck you can press, with a real plucked-string sound
Names any chord you make ("G major chord, bright and happy")
21 chords with finger-by-finger steps
Every note on the staff, and everywhere it's played on the neck
Works without internet

apps.name: Dylan's Bassoon
apps.subtitle: An interactive bassoon fingering chart
description: Every key and hole of a German-system bassoon, both hands, front and back. Tap them to press them (as many as you like) and it tells you which note that plays, or what's closest if it isn't a real fingering.
Or go the other way: pick any note from low B♭ to high D and see exactly how to finger it, in a picture and in plain words, with the other common ways to play it.
features: All 42 notes, from low B♭ to high D, in bass and tenor clef
Press the keys yourself and see what note you get
Half-holes, flick keys and other ways to play each note
Fingerings checked against the International Double Reed Society's chart
Works without internet

apps.name: Dylan's Weather App
apps.subtitle: Live radar and the forecast, at a glance
description: A live, animated weather radar in a soft Windy-style look, with the last hour of rain playing on a loop. Below it: the weather right now, any alerts, the chance of rain hour by hour for the next three days, and the 7-day forecast.
It starts on Fort Lauderdale. Tap the place's name to pick yours, or use where you are. Your place stays on your phone. US places only: the forecast and radar come from the National Weather Service.
features: The last hour of radar, animated, recolored from light rain to severe storms
Right now: temperature, feels like, humidity and wind
Weather alerts for your area
Chance of rain hour by hour, three days ahead
The 7-day forecast
No account, no ads: straight from the National Weather Service

apps.name: Dylan's Daily Torah
apps.subtitle: This week's portion, a section a day
description: This week's Torah portion in English and Hebrew: what happens in it, its four main lessons, its haftarah, where it falls among all 54 portions, and the Hebrew year as a wheel with the moon and the holidays coming up.

Then today: the day's section of the portion, an insight to take into the day, the verse of the day in Hebrew and English, Rashi on it, and a passage of the Talmud that discusses it, each with its full text a tap away.
features: A section a day: the whole portion in a week
Lessons and a daily insight in plain English, written for every portion
The verse of the day in Hebrew and English
Rashi and the Talmud on it, with the full text a tap away
The Hebrew date, the year as a wheel, and the next holidays
Light (old-paper sepia) or dark
apps.internet: Needed the first time each day (for the texts)

apps.name: Dylan's Co-Star
apps.subtitle: Your day and your chart, in the style of Co-Star
description: Your day at a glance, in the spare black-and-white style of the Co-Star app: a line for the day, a short reading, what to do and not do, and the transits behind it, with grainy planet pictures drawn dot by dot.

Below it: your birth chart with the sky right now around the outside, where every planet is today next to where it was when you were born, and the moon's phase. The planets are worked out on your phone from real astronomy, nothing made up.
The first time, type in your birth date, time and place. They stay on your phone.
features: A daily reading from today's real planets and your chart
Do and don't lists, and your transits in plain words
Your birth chart, with the sky right now around it
Every planet now next to where it was at your birth
The moon's phase
Dark or light, like the app
Your birth details stay on your phone
apps.internet: Needed the first time (for the astronomy)

apps.name: Dylan's Tarot
apps.subtitle: Learn to read tarot, in plain English
description: A tarot teacher in your pocket, with the classic 1909 Rider-Waite-Smith deck. Draw a card of the day, lay out a reading and see it read the way a teacher would: each card in its spot, what stands out across the table, famous pairs, and the story put together.

Twelve short lessons take you from the very basics to reading for someone else, and every one of the 78 cards is explained in plain English: what it means right side up and upside down, what's in the picture, and a trick for remembering it.
features: A card of the day
Readings with six spreads, from one card to the Celtic Cross, read aloud like a teacher would
Love, work, money or decision questions
12 short lessons, from the basics up
All 78 cards, each with its meaning, picture and memory trick
Works without internet

apps.name: Dylan's Corkboard
apps.subtitle: South Florida events, and your own reminders
description: A cork board with pages torn off notepads, one page per month. The first board is things to do around South Florida: Greater Fort Lauderdale's big yearly events (the boat show, Winterfest, Tortuga, the air show and more), the Las Olas art fairs, Art Basel, the Delray Affair, Halloween Horror Nights and IBJJF jiu-jitsu tournaments, with a map showing where each one is.
The second board is yours: add your appointments, reminders and birthdays, and they land on the right month's page. They stay on your phone.
features: South Florida's big events, a page per month
A map with a pin for each one, in its month's color
Countdowns for anything coming up this week
Your own appointments, reminders and birthdays
Your reminders stay on your phone
Works without internet

apps.name: Dylan's World Art Show
apps.subtitle: New art from living artists, a piece every minute
description: A gallery wall for your phone or iPad: new hand-made and digital art by living artists from around the world, a new piece every minute, with who made it and where they're from.
It's its own website, kept up to date with new art every day. Open it, then add it to your Home Screen to show it full screen.
features: A new piece every minute
Hand-made and digital art by living artists
Who made it, and where they're from
Full screen from the Home Screen
